headline: Shift Data Center Energy Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, including data centers, to pay for increased generating capacity and related infrastructure costs, aiming to reduce residential electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Senator Louise Lucas, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (with amendments), environmental groups (indirectly).
opponents: Large energy users (data centers, industrial manufacturers).
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed legislation, including HB 1393, that directs regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers and other large users, aiming to prevent these costs from being unfairly passed to residential customers. The bill also allows Dominion Energy to spend more on burying power lines to improve reliability.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report monthly water consumption data to the State Water Control Board, including reclaimed water, to increase transparency and inform water planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental and conservation groups (e.g., Nature Forward), local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Data Center Bills Led 2026 Virginia General Assembly
news_summary: SB 553, among other data center bills, addresses water use transparency by requiring utilities to report how much water data centers consume. This aims to provide communities with clearer insight into local resource use, as such data has often been kept private.

headline: Establish Data Center Siting Rules
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high energy use facilities (HEUF) like data centers, examining noise impacts on nearby residences and schools, and allowing assessment of water, agricultural, and historic resource impacts before approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, homeowner associations, environmental groups, local governments, Del. Josh Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations.
news_headline: Data Center Bills Led 2026 Virginia General Assembly
news_summary: HB 153 introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval. Lawmakers view this as a foundation for stronger future regulations on data center placement and community impact.
